newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INQUIRY RECOMMENDS ROLE CHANGE FOR S.AFRICA'S KWV.
newsitem.headline: INQUIRY RECOMMENDS ROLE CHANGE FOR S.AFRICA'S KWV.

text.p: A committee appointed by government to probe plans by wine co-operative KWV to convert itself into a company has recommended that the Wine and Spirits Control Act be scrapped.

Instead, committee chairman Eckart Kassier told Reuters on Wednesday, the wine industry regulations administered by KWV should be administered by a committee representing the wine trade, producers and government.

Observers said that the recommendation, if accepted by Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom, would overcome the present situation whereby the KWV is in effect "both player and referee" in the wine industry.

Hanekom appointed the committee in January after he had blocked plans by KWV to become a company. He said at the time that the bid would be delayed until he was satisfied that it was in the best interests of the industry.

Kassier said that another committee was still auditing the assets held or controlled by KWV, while the Competition Board was investigating the implications on competition in the wine industry that might result from KWV's proposed restructuring.
KWV management have said they have no immediate plans to float the company.
